Step 1: Compare the masses of the particles involved.  
- A proton has a mass of about 1 atomic mass unit (u).  
- A neutron has a mass of about 1 u.  
- A nucleus contains all the protons and neutrons, so its mass is many times larger than 1 u.  
- An electron has a mass of only about 1/1836 u.  

Step 2: Determine which loss results in the smallest decrease in mass.  
Losing a proton or a neutron reduces the atom’s mass by roughly 1 u. Losing the nucleus removes the bulk of the atom’s mass. Losing an electron removes only a tiny fraction of a u.  

Therefore, the atom loses the least mass if it loses an electron.
